rows.task_text:
Task: Identify floating ice lid
Identify floating ice lid areas in a lake region by analyzing SAR backscatter intensity and optical-derived dark shadow features from Landsat 8, using thresholding on normalized HH band values and masking with optical data to classify frozen, undecided, and floating ice zones.
rows.required_outcome: A three-zone classification (frozen / undecided / floating ice) for the lake region from SAR and optical evidence.
required_constraints: [IMPLICIT] SAR-optical combination logic (threshold classes refined by optical mask)
acceptable_alternatives: Any combination order of SAR classes and optical mask yielding the three zones
underdetermined_aspects: Threshold values; dark-shadow detection criterion
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: SAR HH thresholding + optical dark shadow, three zones

rows.task_text:
Task: Classify coral and sand habitats
Classify benthic habitats (coral, sand, and deep water) in the Belitung region using Lyzenga's water column correction applied to Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, followed by Random Forest and SVM classification on B2_median band, with accuracy assessment from training data.
rows.required_outcome: Classified benthic habitat map (coral / sand / deep water) for Belitung with accuracy assessment from training data.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] Landsat 8 SR; Lyzenga water-column correction; B2_median
acceptable_alternatives: Any Lyzenga implementation; any train/assess split mechanism
failure_conditions: Missing one of the two classifiers
underdetermined_aspects: Training sample provenance; classifier hyperparameters; median-composite period
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: coral/sand/deep-water classification, Lyzenga, RF+SVM, accuracy

rows.task_text:
Task: Calculate sagebrush ecosystem integrity
Calculate the Sagebrush Ecosystem Integrity (SEI) index using simulated aboveground biomass outputs from STEPWAT — specifically sagebrush, perennial forbs/grasses, and annual forbs/grasses — converted to ecological quality (Q) scores via ecoregion-specific cover-biomass relationships (q-curves). It combines these Q scores multiplicatively with existing threat layers (tree encroachment, human modification) to produce a continuous SEI560 metric, then applies Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius (SEI2000), classifies the result into deciles, and reclassifies into three management classes: 'core', 'grow', and 'treat'. Outputs are multi-band Earth Engine image assets containing raw Q layers, SEI560, SEI2000, decile-classified SEI, and 3-class management designations for current and future climate scenarios (RCP45, 2070–2100).
rows.required_outcome: Multi-band assets with raw Q layers, SEI560, SEI2000, decile and 3-class management designations for current and future (RCP45 2070-2100) conditions.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] multiplicative combination with threat layers (tree encroachment, human modification)
[EXPLICIT] SEI560 -> Gaussian 2000 m SEI2000 -> deciles -> core/grow/treat
required_capabilities: Same family as 78050 (sister task, current-state variant)
acceptable_alternatives: Different SOFTWARE implementations of the SAME Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius are acceptable; other kernel types or radii are NOT equivalent substitutes
failure_conditions: Missing threat-layer combination or any stage
underdetermined_aspects: q-curve parameters (data-given)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: q-curves, threats multiply, SEI560/2000, deciles, 3 classes, both scenarios

Task: Extract monthly surface pressure
Extract monthly mean surface pressure from ERA5 reanalysis data for the period 2000–2020 at specific ASOS station locations, computes the average value across 20 years for each month, and exports the results per station.

Stations not matched to grid values

rows.task_text:
Task: Model bear habitat suitability
the workflow models habitat suitability for bears using presence points and environmental predictors, generating a probability map of suitable habitat and a binary potential distribution map. It employs spatial block cross-validation with random forests to train and validate the model, then averages predictions across iterations to produce a final habitat suitability map. Outputs include variable importance, training/testing partitions, and an estimated area of potential distribution in square kilometers.
rows.required_outcome: A final habitat-suitability map (predictions averaged across block-CV iterations) with probability and binary potential-distribution outputs, plus variable importance, train/test partitions, and potential-distribution area in km2.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] presence points + environmental predictors as model inputs
[EXPLICIT] predictions averaged across CV iterations into the final map
[EXPLICIT] outputs: probability map, binary potential distribution, variable importance, train/test partitions, potential-distribution area in km2
acceptable_alternatives: Any block-partition scheme; any defensible binarization rule consistent with the binary map
failure_conditions: Model other than Random Forest substituted
Fold predictions not averaged into a final map
Missing variable importance / partitions / area estimate
underdetermined_aspects: Block size/number; predictor list details; binarization threshold
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: RF + block CV + averaged predictions; two maps + importance + partitions + area km2

rows.task_text:
Task: Estimate forest cover from fractional vegetation
Estimate forest area and percentage cover in Nicaragua for March 2020 using MODIS MCD43A4 surface reflectance data. It applies a spectral mixture analysis (SMA) to derive bare soil, photosynthetic vegetation (PV), and non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV) fractions, then classifies canopy cover where PV > 0.6 and bare < 0.4. Results include printed statistics for estimated forest area in square kilometers and percent forest cover, along with time-series charting of fractional cover from 2017–2020. The output visualizations include SMA results, forest cover maps, and protected areas overlay.
rows.required_outcome: Forest area (km2) and percentage cover for Nicaragua, March 2020, from SMA fractions with stated canopy-cover thresholds, plus fractional-cover time-series charting for 2017-2020 and the stated visualizations.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] MCD43A4 surface reflectance input; Nicaragua; March 2020
[EXPLICIT] SMA yielding bare-soil / PV / NPV fractions
[EXPLICIT] canopy-cover classification rule: PV > 0.6 AND bare < 0.4
[EXPLICIT] outputs: printed forest-area (km2) and percent-cover statistics
[IMPLICIT] fraction-to-forest classification applying the stated thresholds
acceptable_alternatives: Any SMA formulation consistent with the three fractions
failure_conditions: Thresholds not applied as stated (PV>0.6, bare<0.4)
underdetermined_aspects: Endmember spectra (values data-determined)
presentation_requirements: SMA results visualization, forest cover map, protected-areas overlay (all task-stated)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: SMA thresholds PV>0.6/bare<0.4, printed stats, 2017-2020 chart, SMA/forest/protected visualizations; 2020 estimation is the analytical core, 2017-2020 charting is a stated presentation time series

rows.task_text:
Task: Model heating and cooling degree days
the workflow models fuzzy heating and cooling degree days using daily minimum and maximum temperature projections from the CESM1-BGC climate model under historical and RCP scenarios (rcp45, rcp85). It calculates daily mean temperatures, applies fuzzy logic thresholds (with and without 3-day averaging) to estimate building energy demand proxies, and exports annual raster maps of heating and cooling days for 2000 (historical) and 2050 (future projection), including their differences. The outputs are masked to land areas using MODIS land cover data and visualized with custom color palettes.
rows.required_outcome: Annual heating/cooling degree-day rasters for EACH scenario - historical 2000, RCP45 2050, AND RCP85 2050 - together with their required difference maps, land-masked and visualized.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] CESM1-BGC daily min/max under historical + rcp45/rcp85
[EXPLICIT] daily mean temperatures; fuzzy thresholds with and without 3-day averaging
[EXPLICIT] annual rasters for 2000 and 2050 including differences
acceptable_alternatives: Any fuzzy-membership implementation; any differencing arrangement
failure_conditions: Fuzzy logic absent (plain thresholds substituted without basis)
underdetermined_aspects: Fuzzy threshold values; GCM ensemble details; difference-map baseline pairing (the natural reading 2050-minus-2000 is a reasonable route but the task does not fix the baseline)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: fuzzy HDD/CDD, 2000 vs 2050, differences, MODIS mask, palettes

rows.task_text:
Task: Model permafrost thermal state
the workflow models the spatial distribution of permafrost thermal state (ALT - Active Layer Thickness) using kriging interpolation and Random Forest regression. It first performs geostatistical interpolation (kriging) on ALT point data to generate a continuous surface, then combines it with environmental covariates (e.g., soil properties, climate indices, NDVI, NDSI) to train a machine learning model. The final output is a classified raster map of estimated ALT (E), validated through training accuracy metrics and variable importance charts, with results exported as assets and visualized on the map.
rows.required_outcome: Estimated ALT in two related products - the continuous RF-regression ALT surface and the classified raster DERIVED from it - with training accuracy metrics and variable-importance outputs, as stated by the task.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] kriging interpolation of ALT point data
[EXPLICIT] training accuracy metrics + variable importance; asset export
acceptable_alternatives: Any kriging implementation; any classified-bin scheme for ALT
failure_conditions: Continuous ALT surface or its derived classified raster missing
Training accuracy metrics or variable-importance outputs absent
underdetermined_aspects: Kriging parameters; covariate combination specifics; classification bin edges
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: kriging + RF, training accuracy + variable importance, asset export

rows.task_text:
Task: Quantify VIIRS active fire FRP and area
the workflow quantifies monthly VIIRS (VNP14IMGML) active fire radiative power (FRP in MW) and burned area (in km²) at 375 m resolution, disaggregated by spatial overlap with MODIS Aqua FRP, MODIS Terra FRP, and MODIS MCD64A1 burned area within user-selected GFEDv4 basis regions (e.g., Basis 1). It computes four mutually exclusive VIIRS fire metrics: total VIIRS FRP/area (AF), VIIRS FRP/area outside MODIS Aqua FRP (AFnoAqua), outside MODIS burned area (AFnoBA), and outside all MODIS fire observations (AFnoMODIS). These are aggregated via reduceRegions to sum statistics per GFEDv4 polygon and exported as CSV tables containing summed FRP (MW) and area (km²) per 0.25° grid cell (implicitly via polygon-level aggregation over GFED basis region geometry).
rows.required_outcome: CSV tables of summed VIIRS FRP (MW) and burned area (km2) per GFEDv4 basis region under four mutually exclusive fire metrics.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] four metrics: AF, AFnoAqua, AFnoBA, AFnoMODIS (mutually exclusive definitions)
[EXPLICIT] spatial overlap against MODIS Aqua FRP / Terra FRP / MCD64A1
[EXPLICIT] reduceRegions sums per GFEDv4 polygon; CSV export
[IMPLICIT] overlay-exclusion ordering realizing the four definitions
acceptable_alternatives: Any order of exclusion overlays producing identical metric semantics
failure_conditions: Missing any of the four metrics
underdetermined_aspects: 0.25-degree gridding detail (task self-noted 'implicitly')
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: four exclusive metrics, GFED regions, reduceRegions sums, CSV

Task: Monitor maritime activity intensity
Monitor maritime activity intensity in the Port of Singapore using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery by generating a median VV/VH polarisation composite over 2023, visualising backscatter characteristics for vessel detection and sea surface analysis, and quantifying temporal acquisition density via monthly image counts — outputs include clipped composite rasters (VV/VH), a study area boundary layer, summary statistics (total/ascending/descending image counts), and a monthly column chart of image availability.

presentation_requirements: VV/VH backscatter visualisation for vessel/sea-surface analysis (task-stated)

rows.task_text:
Task: Monitor crop health using NDVI time series
Monitor agricultural crop health across Punjab’s agricultural areas using Sentinel-2 Harmonized Surface Reflectance imagery from 2024–2025. It applies cloud masking (via QA60 bit flags), calculates NDVI (B8/B4), EVI, NDRE, and SAVI, generates a monthly NDVI time series chart, produces classified crop health maps (5-tier: Stressed to Very Healthy) based on NDVI thresholds, computes NDVI anomaly for stress detection, exports latest NDVI, mean NDVI, peak NDVI, health classification, and regional NDVI statistics as GeoTIFFs and CSV — all tailored for operational crop stress assessment and seasonal health tracking.
rows.required_outcome: A crop-health monitoring suite over Punjab: masked multi-index imagery, monthly NDVI time series, 5-tier health classification, NDVI anomaly layer, and the stated export set.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] Sentinel-2 Harmonized SR 2024-2025; QA60 cloud mask
[EXPLICIT] monthly NDVI series chart; 5-tier classification from NDVI thresholds
[EXPLICIT] exports: latest/mean/peak NDVI, health classification, regional stats as GeoTIFF+CSV
[IMPLICIT] monthly composite organization; index->classification dependency; anomaly baseline relation
acceptable_alternatives: Any composite/reduce arrangement; any charting mechanism
failure_conditions: Missing cloud mask or any stated index
Missing monthly series / classification / anomaly / any stated export
underdetermined_aspects: 5-tier NDVI threshold values; anomaly baseline period
presentation_requirements: monthly NDVI time-series chart (task-stated presentation requirement)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task lists QA60, four indices, monthly series, 5 tiers, anomaly, full export set

rows.task_text:
Task: Estimate water depth using SDB
Estimate shallow water bathymetry using the Lyzenga's Simple Depth Band Ratio (SDB) method on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2020 to 2022. It applies cloud masking by joining S2_CLOUD_PROBABILITY with S2_SR, computes log-transformed band ratios for blue, green, and red bands, and performs linear regression using in-situ depth points. The model is trained on 80% of the points and validated on 20%, producing a scatter plot of estimated vs. actual depths with R² and RMSE. The final output is a calibrated bathymetric raster map exported to Earth Engine Assets.
rows.required_outcome: A calibrated bathymetric raster (SDB) for the study area, with regression quality reported (R2, RMSE) on an 80/20 split.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] linear regression on in-situ depth points; 80/20 train/validation
[EXPLICIT] scatter with R2/RMSE; asset export of calibrated raster
acceptable_alternatives: Any regression execution route (in-EE reduce or export-train-apply)
underdetermined_aspects: Regression coefficients (data-determined); exact ratio pairing
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: join, log band ratios, regression 80/20, R2/RMSE, asset export

rows.task_text:
Task: Analyze aerosol reflectance over AOI
Analyze mean aerosol reflectance in the B1 band (ultra-blue) of Sentinel-2 imagery over a small AOI from 2016-09-01 to 2017-09-30. It filters the Sentinel-2 image collection by date and region, clips each image to the AOI, computes the mean value of band B1 using reduceRegion, and appends this statistic as a property ('Aerosol_Mean') to each image. The output includes the size of the filtered collection, metadata of individual images, and visualization of up to 12 images using a false-color composite (B8, B3, B4), enabling visual inspection of surface and atmospheric features.
rows.required_outcome: Per-image B1 (ultra-blue) mean statistics appended as image properties over the AOI period, plus collection-size/metadata reporting and up-to-12 false-color previews.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] report collection size and per-image metadata
acceptable_alternatives: Any property-append mechanism; any preview batching
underdetermined_aspects: AOI geometry source; visualization params beyond band combo
presentation_requirements: up-to-12 false-color previews (task-stated; presentation requirement, not planning evidence)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: reduceRegion B1 mean appended per image; size/metadata; 12 false-color

rows.task_text:
Task: Calculate sagebrush ecosystem integrity
Calculate future Sagebrush Ecosystem Integrity (SEI) using Method 1 from Doherty et al. 2022: it computes scaled percent change in STEPWAT-simulated biomass (sage, perennial grass, annual forb/grass) under climate scenarios (RCP45, 2070–2100), multiplies these delta-S values by current smoothed percent cover layers (sage560m, perennialG560m, annualG560m) from RAP (Rangeland Analysis Platform), converts to Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) using ecoregion-specific curves (Great Basin, Intermountain, Plains), integrates resources and threats multiplicatively (Q1–Q5) to produce continuous SEI560, applies Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius to yield SEI2000, classifies into deciles, then reclassifies into three management classes (core/grow/treat), and exports a multi-band GEE Image Asset containing all intermediate and final layers (Q1raw–Q5sc3) per GCM.
rows.required_outcome: A multi-band asset per GCM containing Q layers, SEI560, SEI2000, decile classes, and three management classes for future scenarios.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] Method 1 (Doherty 2022): delta-S from STEPWAT biomass under RCP45 2070-2100
[EXPLICIT] multiply delta-S by RAP smoothed cover layers; ecoregion-specific curves (Great Basin/Intermountain/Plains)
[EXPLICIT] Q1-Q5 multiplicative integration -> SEI560 -> Gaussian 2000 m -> SEI2000 -> deciles -> core/grow/treat
[EXPLICIT] multi-band GEE asset with all intermediate + final layers
[IMPLICIT] delta-S computation; integration order as specified by method
acceptable_alternatives: Different SOFTWARE implementations of the SAME Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius are acceptable; other kernel types or radii are NOT equivalent substitutes
failure_conditions: Missing any method stage (delta-S, curve application, Q integration, smoothing, classifications)
underdetermined_aspects: Curve parameter values (data-given); GCM count handling
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task text IS the method specification; all stages explicit

rows.task_text:
Task: Analyze groundwater storage time series
Extract and analyzes monthly groundwater storage (GWS) time series from the NASA GLDAS CLSM model over a defined polygonal region in Iran (approximately spanning longitudes 43.67–63.09°E and latitudes 24.94–39.79°N) for the period 2003–2024. It computes monthly mean GWS_tavg values, generates two charts — one showing spatially averaged (over the polygon) monthly GWS evolution, and another showing point-based time series at two user-defined locations (loc1 and loc2) — and exports the full monthly stack as a clipped, multi-band GeoTIFF to Google Drive. The workflow includes date sequence generation, image collection filtering and reduction, metadata annotation (system:time_start/end/index), null-band filtering, and visualization/export setup.
rows.required_outcome: Monthly GWS time-series outputs per the task's TWO charts - (a) polygon-averaged monthly GWS evolution, (b) point-based time series at the two user-defined locations - plus a clipped multi-band GeoTIFF export.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] monthly means; two charts (polygon-average + two point series)
acceptable_alternatives: Any month-loop implementation; any charting mechanism
failure_conditions: Missing monthly series or either chart type
underdetermined_aspects: User-defined point coordinates (task says loc1/loc2 by user)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: polygon + two points, monthly means, charts, clipped GeoTIFF

rows.task_text:
Task: Classify benthic habitats using Random Forest
the workflow performs atmospheric correction using Dark Object Subtraction (DOS) on a satellite image over Misool, then applies a Random Forest classifier to classify benthic habitats into four classes (e.g., water, vegetation, sand, coral) using deglinted bands and a derived index (DII23), based on training samples from ROI_Sunglint. The output is a classified benthic map exported to Google Drive.
rows.required_outcome: A four-class benthic habitat classification over Misool from DOS-corrected imagery, exported to Drive.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] RF classifier; FOUR classes (task names water/vegetation/sand/coral as examples - count is hard, exact label set not exhaustively fixed)
[EXPLICIT] deglinted bands + DII23 index as features; ROI_Sunglint training samples
acceptable_alternatives: Any DOS variant; any sampling mechanism from ROI
failure_conditions: Missing RF stage or DII23 feature
underdetermined_aspects: DII23 formula details (named, not specified); confirmation of the exact four-label set (task gives example names)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: DOS, RF four classes, deglinted bands + DII23, ROI training, Drive export

rows.task_text:
Task: Assess drought severity using VHI
Compute the Vegetation Health Index (VHI) over the Irrawaddy Basin using Landsat 7 surface temperature and NDVI data from 2013 to 2020. It derives VHI by combining the Temperature Condition Index (TCI) and Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) during the hot season (March–May) each year, masks areas with NDVI > 0.2 to focus on vegetated regions, and identifies drought-affected areas where VHI < 20. The outputs include annual VHI raster maps exported to Google Drive and CSV files summarizing the total drought-affected area in square kilometers for each year.
rows.required_outcome: Annual VHI rasters and a CSV of yearly drought-affected area (km2) for the Irrawaddy Basin.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] VHI = TCI+VCI combination, hot season Mar-May
[EXPLICIT] NDVI>0.2 vegetation mask; VHI<20 drought flag
[EXPLICIT] Drive rasters + CSV of yearly affected km2
acceptable_alternatives: Any normalization baseline (underdetermined); any area-summation route
failure_conditions: Vegetation or drought threshold not applied
underdetermined_aspects: TCI/VCI normalization baseline period (min/max reference)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: TCI+VCI, NDVI>0.2 mask, VHI<20, yearly km2 CSV

rows.task_text:
Task: Classify ice and water types
Classify pixel-level surface types in lakes into four categories: water, clear ice, opaque ice, and snow using Landsat TOA reflectance data. It trains a Random Forest model on labeled training samples with spectral predictors and validates it temporally by splitting data by year (before/after 2019), ultimately producing a trained classification model for cryospheric surface mapping.
rows.required_outcome: Pixel-level four-class (water / clear ice / opaque ice / snow) classified surface results produced by a trained RF model validated temporally by pre/post-2019 splits (a trained model alone without classified results is incomplete).
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] RF on labeled samples with spectral predictors
acceptable_alternatives: Any feature set drawn from spectral predictors; any split implementation
underdetermined_aspects: Exact predictor list; hyperparameters; sample sizes; delivery/export form of the classified results (task requires generation for cryospheric surface mapping but specifies no Drive/GeoTIFF/asset format)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: four classes, RF on labels, before/after-2019 validation

rows.task_text:
Task: Detect active fires with GOES-17
Process GOES-17 ABI Level 2 Multichannel Cloud and Moisture Imagery (MCMIPF) data to generate true-color and false-color visualizations by applying scale/offset corrections, adding a synthetic green band via spectral blending, and scaling for visualization. It then integrates Fire Detection and Characterization (FDCF) data by mapping confidence values to fire mask codes, filtering for high-confidence fire pixels (≥0.3), and overlaying them on the MCMIPF imagery. The output is a time-lapse visualization collection where active fires are highlighted in red over corrected multispectral imagery, enabling spatiotemporal monitoring of wildfires.
rows.required_outcome: A time-lapse visualization collection: corrected GOES-17 multispectral imagery with high-confidence fire pixels overlaid in red.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] synthetic green band via spectral blending
[EXPLICIT] red fire overlay on corrected imagery; time-lapse collection output
acceptable_alternatives: Any blending formula (task says 'spectral blending' without coefficients)
failure_conditions: Confidence filter absent or wrong threshold
Fire overlay missing from output collection
underdetermined_aspects: Synthetic-green coefficients (standard blends exist; task unfixed)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: scale/offset, synthetic green, FDCF >=0.3, red overlay, time-lapse

rows.task_text:
Task: Extract daily height data
Process the RTMA (Real-Time Mesoscale Analysis) dataset to extract daily mean values of the 'HGT' (height) variable from January 1, 2020, to January 31, 2020. It creates an ImageCollection where each image represents the mean height for a single day, renamed by date, and includes time metadata. The output is a time-series collection of daily height fields over North America at high spatial resolution.
rows.required_outcome: A time-series ImageCollection of daily mean 'HGT' (height) fields over January 2020, each image dated and carrying time metadata.
required_constraints: [EXPLICIT] daily mean of HGT per day
[EXPLICIT] images renamed by date with time metadata
required_capabilities: Daily temporal aggregation (each output image = one day's HGT spatial field)
acceptable_alternatives: Any per-day aggregation implementation (grouped reduce vs looped composites)
failure_conditions: Missing date renaming or time metadata
underdetermined_aspects: Regional clipping details (dataset native extent may suffice)
rows.gold_chain_audit: PENDING-STAGE-2-STYLE (chains-as-reference only; A-group chains are GEE reference, never gold source)
rows.evidence: task: daily mean HGT, Jan 2020, renamed by date, time metadata
